best_network.summary: Vodafone is likely best here, with a clear line of sight to a site 0.1 km east confirmed by Ofcom's licence register. EE and O2 also have clear lines to sites 0.1 km away; EE and O2 operators are inferred from crowd-sourced data rather than confirmed by Ofcom's licence register [network_comparison][los_ee][los_o2][los_vodafone]. Three has a site 190 m south with a small terrain margin, so its signal is likely weakened, not necessarily lost [los_three].

rule_based.label: Based on data, not yet reviewed by agents
rule_based.rule: Operators ranked by line of sight from this point to their nearest identified site (clear, then marginal, then blocked); clear lines by distance, obstructed ones by how far the ground rises above the line.
rule_based.text: Likely best network here: Vodafone, with a clear line of sight to a site 0.1 km east (confirmed by Ofcom's licence register). Also a clear line: EE (0.1 km) and O2 (0.1 km).

limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed where not confirmed; Ofcom figures are area-level.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.

critiques.reason: The belief is well-supported by strong speed measurements (1425 tests in cell, 1065 within 1 km, 5033 in neighbouring cells) all showing speeds well above UK median, clear line of sight to three operators' sites within 112 m confirmed by Ofcom licence register, and no active severe weather warnings. The evidence does not rely mainly on weak items; the weak line of sight for Three does not undermine the overall conclusion.
